@graph.name: Pail and Bucket Palletizer
@graph.description: A pail palletizer, also called a bucket palletizer, is a robotic system that picks filled, lidded pails from the end of a filling line and stacks them onto pallets in a stable, repeatable pattern. TRF Industrial Automation evaluates pail applications on TRFCobot, TRFCompact and TRFSpeed within their published case weights, or as a custom palletizer, and the right model is defined by your line setup and speed.

mainEntity.name: Is a Bucket Palletizer the Same as a Pail Palletizer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Bucket and pail are two names for the same container, and the palletizing questions are identical: filled weight, lid and handle design, line rate and pallet pattern. TRF treats both as one application and selects the platform, the end-of-arm tool and the pattern for your specific container.

mainEntity.name: What Payload Does a Palletizing Robot Need for Filled Pails?

acceptedAnswer.text: The robot must carry the filled pail plus the end-of-arm tool, and for multipick, the combined weight of the pails. Published case weights are up to about 22 lb for TRFCobot, 44 lb for TRFCompact and 66 lb for TRFSpeed. TRF validates the payload with your filled pail. A pail heavier than that range is not a standard-platform application; it is evaluated as a custom palletizer project after the application review.

mainEntity.name: Can One Palletizer Handle Different Pail Sizes and Pallet Patterns?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, within the validated application. TRF palletizing platforms run multiple recipes and pallet patterns, so the same pail palletizer can handle more than one pail size or pattern. Each size is validated with its end-of-arm tool and pattern during project engineering, and a wide size range may need an adjustable or interchangeable tool, which is defined in the application review.

mainEntity.name: Can a Pail Palletizer Fit a Plant With Limited Floor Space?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often, yes. TRFCobot has a small footprint for areas where a traditional robotic cell is hard to install, and TRFCompact brings an industrial robot into a compact, standardized cell for brownfield plants that add a pail line where space is already committed. Layout, reach and operator access to full pallets are confirmed for each installation.

mainEntity.name: Can a Robotic Palletizer Operate Below Freezing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, with TRFSubzero, the TRF palletizer for areas below 32°F, built for frozen food, ice cream and other below-freezing areas. If your pails are palletized in a freezer, the rate, payload and end-of-arm tool are validated per application, like any other pail line.

mainEntity.name: How Much Does a Pail Palletizer Cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cost depends on the platform, line speed, filled pail weight, end-of-arm tool, pallet handling and conveyor integration. As a reference, list prices are US$ 120,000 for the TRFCobot Dual, US$ 180,000 for the TRFCompact Dual and US$ 350,000 for the TRFSpeed 100, EX Works Lenexa, Kansas, installation not included. The robotic palletizer cost page explains each factor.

mainEntity.name: What Information Should I Prepare to Size a Pail Palletizer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bring your pail sizes and filled weights, the lid and handle design, the line rate, your pallet size and target height, the number of filling lines and a drawing of the floor space. A TRF Sales Engineer uses this data to screen TRFCobot, TRFCompact, TRFSpeed or a custom palletizer, and the payback calculator gives you a first estimate.
